transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-05-28
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Lena (CTO - Sable), Marcus (Head Infra), Nadia (Security Lead), Owen (Network)

Summary: quick discovery focused on private VPC deployment options, networking patterns (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region constraints and security requirements for Sable Payments' PII workloads. Agreed to follow up with deep-dive on network routing and a security pack.

Topics: Private VPC architecture, Private endpoints, VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region/residency constraints, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, latency/cost tradeoffs for dedicated vs hosted, deployment runbook for POC.

Transcript:
00:00 - Ethan: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll keep this to 45, i think, to respect time. i'm ethan from redwood, our se priya and carlos are on too. uh lena, marcus, nadia, owen, thanks for being here.
00:12 - Lena: thanks, yeah appreciate it. we just want to understand private deployment options, network requirements, and what the integration surface looks like, right, for payments data.
00:20 - Priya: great, at a high level we offer three surfaces: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private which is the vpc/on-prem option. today we'll focus on private. we'll cover control plane placement, private endpoints, peering options and any region constraints you might have.
00:35 - Marcus: quick top-level --- our requirements: all cardholder data and PII must stay inside our AWS account in us-east-1; minimal egress; SOC2 compliance; we also need kms integration with our HSM. latency target is 100ms p95 for our transaction enrichment use case.
00:51 - Priya: good, that helps. two quick clarifications: by "private" do you mean customer-managed VPC with a private control plane in your account, or do you want a fully on-prem bundle?
00:58 - Lena: customer-managed VPC in our aws account, ideally peered, with private endpoints. no on-prem right now.
01:05 - Carlos: okay so options in aws: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints), or transit gateway. each has tradeoffs: peering is simple but requires routing and can be messy cross-account; privateLink isolates and avoids route table changes; transit gateway is for scale/multi-vpc.
01:20 - Owen: for us eas-1 is the only allowed region for data residency. are there constraints on where the control plane runs? we can't have control plane in another region.
01:28 - Priya: the private control plane can be deployed into your specified region (us-east-1). we do an initial setup where Redwood's operator creates control plane resources in your account or we provide manifest for your infra team to apply.
01:40 - Owen: and the data path for inference, is that entirely inside our VPC? we need assurance tokens and no public internet egress for request/response.
01:48 - Priya: yes the data plane for private is inside your VPC; requests go to private endpoints we provision or you provision, and traffic never leaves your network. the control plane has narrow outbound to our control services for management, which can be tunneled through an egress proxy if needed.
02:00 - Nadia: about kms: we need to use our existing AWS KMS CMKs backed by our HSM. can redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS so keys never leave account?
02:10 - Priya: we support customer KMS integration; the recommendation is to use an external key encryption for secrets and to provision the model encryption keys under your CMK. we will share the integration doc.
02:18 - Marcus: ok great. what about audit logs and access logs? we need full request traces, token-level audit, and long retention for litigation hold.
02:26 - Carlos: we can emit audit logs to your account (CloudWatch / S3) and set retention. Redwood's private deployment ships an agent that forwards structured logs to your logging endpoint; we also support syslog and S3 buckets for raw traces.
02:38 - Lena: network-wise we use VPC peering today for some prod services, but security prefs lean to PrivateLink because we want minimal route exposure. pricing of endpoints vs peering?
02:47 - Priya: PrivateLink has hourly interface endpoint costs and data processing charges; VPC peering is free but cross-az/region egress costs can apply and you must manage route tables. For low-latency critical flows PrivateLink is often preferred for isolation. We'll model cost for your expected token volume in the follow up.
03:05 - Owen: what's the recommended subnet and security group pattern? we're locking down subnets to only allow specific CIDRs and egress through NAT; will redwood require public subnets?
03:13 - Priya: no public subnets required. Data plane compute will live in private subnets. For the control plane, management components may need egress for updates but we can route through your NAT or proxy. We'll provide a checklist: required ports, SG rules, and route table entries.
03:27 - Marcus: we're also considering dedicated (reserved capacity) rather than private fully; how do they compare? dedicated gives us predictable throughput but it's still hosted. private gives us full VPC isolation but more ops on our side.
03:38 - Ethan: exactly. dedicated is our managed reserved pools in Redwood's infra with enterprise tenancy, so less ops but data passes through our managed network (though encrypted). Private is fully inside your account, so best for compliance but you own more setup.
03:50 - Lena: for PCI scope reduction it's better if we keep traffic in our VPC. any recommendations about model updates and rollouts? we need controlled rollouts and the ability to pin model versions.
03:58 - Carlos: we support model pinning and can do canary rollouts within your private environment. updates to runtime are coordinated and we provide a rollout plan.
04:06 - Nadia: encryption in transit and at rest? TLS mandatory, and we need to enforce mutual TLS for the control plane APIs.
04:13 - Priya: yes TLS 1.2/1.3 enforced; mutual-TLS for some control endpoints is supported, and we can add client cert rotation in your PKI. We'll include configuration examples.
04:24 - Owen: any constraints with cross-region failover? we want active-passive in another region (us-west-2) for DR but can't replicate data. can we deploy control plane in us-east-1 and fail over compute to another region in emergencies?
04:36 - Priya: cross-region compute is possible but data residency rules will block automatic replication. For DR you can run standby resources in us-west-2 but keep data-only artifacts in us-east-1; we can configure routing policies to failover but you'll need to accept some latency/cost tradeoffs. We'll detail options.
04:52 - Marcus: let's talk throughput; our peak is 2000 rps during settlement windows, average is 250 rps. what sizing and GPU counts are needed?
05:01 - Priya: we'll want to run a benchmark with your prompt patterns; but rough estimate: with batching and quantized models we can get high throughput on a few GPUs; for 2k rps you might need multiple nodes and autoscale. we'll propose sizing after we run a small perf test.
05:18 - Lena: can we run a pilot for two weeks to validate latency and cost?
05:23 - Ethan: yes, pilot is our normal path. for private we provision a limited POC in your account or we send IaC for you to deploy. we'll grant telemetry and show cost/latency dashboards in Redwood Console.
05:33 - Nadia: final question, any SOC2 artifacts you can share? we need the report and any pen test summaries.
05:38 - Ethan: yes, we'll send SOC2 Type II, ISO docs, and our pen test summary. Also the KMS/HSM integration guide.
05:46 - Lena: ok that's helpful. seems like Private with PrivateLink may be our preferred pattern; next step deep-dive with Marcus and Owen on network design.
05:55 - Ethan: perfect. quick recap then next steps...
06:02 - Ethan: recap: 1) Redwood to share Private Deployment architecture doc + network checklist + security pack. 2) schedule technical deep-dive with Marcus/Owen next week. 3) Sable to share compliance requirements and any specific egress/proxy constraints. 4) we'll set up pilot plan and benchmark.
06:20 - Marcus: sounds good, thanks.
06:24 - Lena: thanks everyone.
06:27 - Ethan: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links.

References mentioned: Private deployment architecture doc (link to be shared), SOC2 report, KMS integration guide, cost model spreadsheet (to be shared).

Action items (captured in call): Ethan - send architecture doc + checklist; Priya - schedule network deep-dive; Nadia - provide compliance scope; Redwood - provision pilot manifest or IaC; Customer - confirm us-east-1-only constraints and provide estimated token volume per day.

End of transcript.
